doc.title: Carmen Leggio interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998

title: Photos: Overseas Press Club and the narrow Metropole stage
summary: Showing photos, he describes the Metropole's long stage above the bar and trios without bass.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Did you bring some stuff that you wanted to talk about or show us?
Now here’s Frank Dunlop. I played with my own group at the Overseas Press Club in New York and Frank Dunlop was on that.
We’ll take another shot of this when we’re done too.
That was the Overseas Press Club. And then this was John Bunch, this was the Metropole, remember Roy Burns?
Oh now I’ve heard about this stage, this very narrow long stage.
Right that’s it. © Fillius Jazz Archive -19-
I’m so glad to see this picture.
Yeah. That’s what it was. There was an upright piano against the wall.

Right. The bar — yeah we were in the bar there, then there was an opening where the bartenders were and then the bar. And I won’t mention names, but one guy, a trombone player, one day he was wiped out. And he fell and he dangled. Like he was holding on to the bar and his feet were on the stage. It was too much. I won’t mention names, no.
It must have been a workout for the piano player too, with no bass.

No. We played without basses. The trios were without basses. So the piano players had to have a good left hand. See and John Bunch, Marty Napoleon — quite a few — Dick Wellstood, they had good left hands. This was the Maynard Ferguson. I’ll put this back in order. And I can let you have it.
